questions.question: What structural and evidentiary gates does the final RAG pass apply?
options: Permission filtering, supersedure filtering, content-hash deduplication, and faithfulness checking
A larger embedding model, a higher temperature, and a longer context window
Only a human review after the answer has been sent
A single cosine-similarity threshold with no source metadata
questions.explanation: The final pass applies pre-filter, supersedure, content deduplication, and then faithfulness checking. Together they catch stale, mis-tagged, and over-extrapolated answers.

questions.question: What does Pass 2 catch for the three RAG failure-shape scenarios?
options: Only the adjacent-topic extrapolation
The stale policy and mis-tagged duplicate, but not the adjacent-topic extrapolation
All three, because structural metadata proves every answer claim
None, because gates are applied only after generation
questions.explanation: Structural gates remove superseded chunks and duplicate content. They cannot tell that a permitted, current employee policy has been extrapolated to contractors.

questions.question: What does Pass 3 do when the contractor policy answer contains unsupported contractor claims?
options: It cites the employee chunk with higher confidence
It silently rewrites the answer from the nearest current policy
It returns ABSTAINED because the faithfulness gate finds unsupported terms
It promotes the claim because the retrieved chunk is in scope
questions.explanation: faithfulness_check requires every content-bearing term in each claim to appear in the retrieved text. Contractors is absent from the employee chunk, so the pass abstains.

questions.question: Which gate removes the 2019 IT Security Policy v3.1 chunk?
options: gate_content_dedup
gate_pre_filter
faithfulness_check
gate_supersedure
questions.explanation: The stale chunk has superseded_by set to the v5.0 URL. gate_supersedure filters any chunk whose superseded_by is not None.

questions.question: How does gate_content_dedup catch the Atlas copy with an internal permission tag?
options: It hashes content and drops a non-confidential chunk whose hash matches a confidential canonical chunk
It trusts the internal tag and returns the copy as the canonical source
It deletes every duplicate before checking permissions
It compares only source URLs, so identical text at another URL remains
questions.explanation: The gate builds canonical hashes from chunks permitted to confidential users. A matching chunk without that role is treated as the mis-tagged duplicate and removed.

questions.question: Why does faithfulness_check reject the contractor claim from the employee policy chunk?
options: The chunk is stale, even though its date is current
The content-bearing term contractors is not present in the retrieved employee text
The user role is not allowed to read the policy
The query contains more than two terms
questions.explanation: The employee chunk is current and permitted, but it says employees, not contractors. The extractive faithfulness gate catches that unsupported noun instead of allowing confident extrapolation.
